If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 2–5% in early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 2–5% in early horizon (1–7 days) to counteract pessimism.  
In mid-horizon (8–15 days), if sentiment swings from positive to negative, shift forecast downward by 3–7% to reflect sentiment reversal.  
In late-horizon (16–30 days), if sentiment remains neutral (0.33–0.67), apply a 1–3% downward bias to align with historical mean decay.  
If sentiment is positive but forecast is over 10% above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% in late horizon to prevent overfitting.  
If sentiment is negative but forecast is below 10% of recent history, increase forecast by 5–10% in late horizon to avoid underestimation.
